implementation_notes: No language offers spaghetti code as a feature, so there is nothing to configure and nothing to call. The detector is structural and computable: count the nonlocal exits per function (jumps to labels outside the immediately enclosing construct, `break`/`continue` that cross more than one level, exceptions thrown for control flow, shared flag variables read in distant blocks) and the maximum nesting depth. Anything with more than a couple of nonlocal edges per function has a control graph the source does not express. The remedy follows the count: labels and jumps become structured constructs (guard clauses, labelled breaks, an explicit state machine), flag variables become one enumeration, and a blob-shaped dependency graph is fixed by inverting the dependency — not by reindenting. Where the jump is a legitimate single forward early exit, leave it; the rule that matters is no backward jumps and no jumps into a block.
idiom_name: no language support: this is a finding, not a construct
pitfalls: Counting `goto`s is not enough: modern spaghetti is produced by exception-as-control-flow, shared flags and dependency cycles, none of which use the keyword.
Extracting short functions without changing the control flow produces many short unreadable functions.
Rewriting from scratch without characterisation tests discards the implicit specification, bugs included.
